title: It’s Time for Las Vegas to Reinvent Itself Again. This Time as the Newest Amsterdam.

content_html_sanitized:
Quiz: What are the two words that you are very likely to hear in Amsterdam, but very unlikely to hear in Las Vegas?

 

“Over tourism”, although Vegas gets roughly five times as many visitors as Amsterdam. (40 million vs 8 million), Amsterdam is one of the smallest major capitals in the world, and it really seems overcrowded.

 

Now for an easy quiz: What is Amsterdam most famous for? Well, for a city with some of the greatest art museums in the world, a rich history dating back 750 years, great architecture, a world class symphony orchestra, the answer is obviously Cannabis, marijuana, wiet, weed, and 150 “coffee shops” that also sell coffee! That has to be a bit frustrating.

 

Thirty some odd years ago, when I first visited there it was still suffering economically from the aftermath of the Second World War, and there were lots of empty stores and “squats” in prime real estate.

 

Consequently, there were hundreds of coffee shops where people could buy and smoke cannabis, usually hashish. American and Canadian cannabis aficionados made pilgrimages, and American Drug Czars went there to add authenticity to their lies.

 

Today, real estate prices are soaring. Great restaurants are opening, but people still come from around the world from Prohibitionist countries, and even from the US, because there’s something about freedom in the air. Vegas may like to call itself “Sin City”, but it’s really Freedom City.

 

Meanwhile, in Las Vegas, one of the only two “Cannabis Consumption Lounges” closed recently because of the sort of unrealistic restrictions that have made such a mess of cannabis legalization in the U.S.

See Nevada’s first cannabis consumption lounge shuttered

 

Consequently, there are lots of places to buy weed, but almost no place to smoke it. The casinos that mostly still allow gamblers to smoke tobacco at the tables, are afraid of losing their gaming licenses,  if they allow federally illegal cannabis to be used anywhere on site.

 

I have no doubt that they would be happy to have happy people smoking joints along with cigars, because the casino business is hurting, as is tourism generally. There are multiple reasons for this, but it seems unlikely that it will turn around soon..

 

Public use and consumption of marijuana is prohibited, except in a licensed marijuana consumption lounge. It is illegal to use or consume marijuana on a public street or in public buildings, including hotel rooms and casinos, as well as anywhere on federal property, including the airport. Frankly, this really is ridiculous.

 

The obvious solution is to let customers at marijuana retail stores smoke onsite, as they do in Amsterdam, and in almost every town in the Netherlands, but it would require a change in state laws or regulations for “cannabis consumption lounges.

 

After all, restaurants and bars allow customers to drink alcohol onsite. People who want a more upscale experience can go to cannabis lounges, i. e. restaurants that cater to cannabis lovers.

See The Nevada Bar Association on Cannabis Consumption Lounges

 

Plus, there is a parallel trend. More people are switching from alcohol to cannabis.

Two Years Since the End of the Pandemic, Cannabis Continues Replacing Alcohol Socially

 

And this also works with another change in Vegas. It has been twenty five years since entertainment revenues exceeded gaming revenues in Vegas. Now it is roughly 60%, and this is likely to accelerate as more and more of the entertainment industry moves from Los Angeles to Las Vegas. And in the techie world “A I” doesn’t stand for Alcohol Intelligence.

 

Quiz: Do musicians and comedians use cannabis? Who knew?

 

And if the time is right for Vegas, it is also right for the cannabis industry. Because of excessive taxation and over regulation, as demonstrated by the fiasco with the “Cannabis Consumption Lounges”, cannabis legalization has been a major economic disaster.

 

So the cannabis industry and Las Vegas need each other. Amsterdam may be a little embarrassed by the source of its fame, but it’s not embarrassed by hundreds of millions in revenue.

 

Besides, Nevada is also just next door to the largest cannabis market in the world: California, and there are plenty of “cannabis consumption lounges” there.

 

And the only thing that’s really embarrassing in Vegas is losing money.
